extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department chairs, faculty, and mathematics-education reform stakeholders (MER members, program directors)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for evaluating and designing mathematics-department activities (service courses, calculus reform, teaching excellence, technology integration, interdisciplinary programs, graduate education, minority enhancement, K-12 outreach, and departmental partnerships).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of service courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Service courses (e.g., lower-division calculus) should serve the university by providing important foundations for other majors; reforming these courses is an important contribution to the university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time and resources to reform service courses because most students in these classes are not mathematics majors. Ensure content is relevant to the needs of other departments rather than using such courses primarily as gatekeeping devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of requirements (anti-weed-out practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using mathematics requirements (e.g., calculus) primarily to trim majors in other departments by expecting high failure rates to reduce enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report flags this as an inappropriate way for other departments to handle overcrowding; departments should examine fairness and intent of requirements rather than relying on attrition as a selection mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional engagement with non-university community
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether departments have systematic institutional links with local school districts, statewide initiatives, textbook committees, and community organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although individual faculty often serve the community, departments should consider supporting and institutionalizing outreach efforts (beyond isolated faculty activity) to increase impact and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty diversity (gender and minority representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess demographic composition of faculty; many departments show over-representation of white men and low percentages of women (5–10% tenure-track) and very few faculty of color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track percentages (e.g., women averaged 10.5% in sampled departments), implement recruitment strategies (contacts, alumni), and monitor progress relative to national averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate student diversity and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate representation of women and minorities among graduate students and retention/completion metrics (e.g., completion of Ph.D. / number of first year students ≈ 40–50%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that graduate-level representation is higher than faculty but still low for people of color; use targeted recruitment strategies to build future faculty candidate pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and impact of qualifying exams
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying exams are a difficult hurdle influencing retention and recruitment; some chairs prefer admitting students who can pass their exams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine whether qualifying exams' content and role align with program goals, and consider their effect on diversity and student stress. Potentially reconsider core course vs. exam emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate calculus reform fidelity and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting reform calculus materials (e.g., Harvard Calculus), ensure the curriculum covers essential topics (concern: some felt 'they don’t even include coverage of the Central Limit Theorem!').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance appreciation for real-world relevance with coverage completeness; departments often modify adopted materials to fit departmental content expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural aspects of calculus reform (class size and staffing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful reform often requires structural changes such as smaller classes and appropriate staffing; budget constraints may limit such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set explicit targets (e.g., Penn State committing to sections ≤35 students), plan for staffing/training needs, and recognize resource limitations when scaling reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor preparedness / mathematical maturity to teach reform materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform curricula may require more 'mathematical maturity' to teach; departments must assess whether instructors are prepared to deliver new approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide faculty development, create faculty deliberation processes (e.g., Penn State faculty meeting bi-monthly for a year) before wide adoption, and ensure adequate support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of departmental deliberation and consensus-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum changes benefit from sustained faculty discussion and shared evidence from peer departments ('discussing advantages and disadvantages... gave him the sense that he was not isolated').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host internal meetings, share external experiences, and use network workshops to build consensus and inform decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching excellence policies and peer evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments should develop policies and initiatives to promote excellence in teaching, including peer evaluation and supports for individual development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use workshops, collaborative sessions, and internet follow-ups to share practices; aim to develop departmental policies supportive of teaching as a valued activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development for instructors (teaching resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide faculty with information and resources (workshop sessions, TA training programs, mentoring) to improve teaching effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Rutgers' TA training program and MER-hosted sessions; ongoing mentoring during initial teaching assignments is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of technology into curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt technology (graphing calculators, software like Mathematica/Maple, 'smart' classrooms) to allow exploration of complex, realistic problems and dynamic visualization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure students have hands-on access (labs, teaching labs), avoid purely demonstration-based use, and accompany technology adoption with formative evaluation of learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical appraisal of technology (not a crutch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the debate that technology can be a crutch preventing conceptual development versus enabling quicker access to complex problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host balanced workshops on policy and pedagogy related to technology; evaluate impacts empirically rather than assuming benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary involvement and control over math taught across campus
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians should stay involved in mathematics taught in other departments (e.g., statistics taught across campus) to maintain quality and appropriate mathematical control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceptualize 'vertical' (depth) and 'horizontal' (breadth) components of math education and explore just-in-time delivery models for contextual learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and logistics of interdisciplinary programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary courses/programs require careful logistical planning (agreements with other departments, conceptualization) and may be inhibited by logistical constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-institutional workshops to conceptualize large-scale proposals (e.g., NSF proposals) and create mechanisms to sustain interdisciplinary collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate preparation for the changing job market
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to dwindling academic jobs by preparing graduate students with broader skills: more teaching opportunities, teaching-methods workshops, applied mathematics training, and publication support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer TA training, supervised teaching experiences, create Master's programs in applied math where appropriate, and support students to both teach and publish before graduation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate teaching opportunities and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide graduate students with substantive teaching experience (e.g., lecturing calculus), mentoring, and courses/workshops on teaching to improve marketability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions that offer structured TA training or supervised teaching report better preparedness for job markets; track placement outcomes to assess effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination of qualifying exams' content and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether qualifying exams focus departmental effort on the right mathematics content and consider if they align with broader educational goals (including diversity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss core course content vs. exam preparation, and consider convening workshops to examine exam standards and their interaction with recruitment of underrepresented groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate mobility and postdoctoral/adjunct strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitate graduate student exchanges, visiting research presentations, and adjunct/postdoc placements at other universities to broaden experience and improve job prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage short-term exchanges and visiting positions as ways to build networks and teaching records; use departmental and inter-university programs to enable such mobility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design elements of minority enhancement programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective minority retention programs (Treisman-type: Emerging Scholars, Project Excel, MAP) are framed as honors courses, selective invitation, include intensive study workshops (three 2-hour sessions/week), TA-supported collaborative problem-solving, challenging material, and community-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key components: high expectations, structured study groups, TA facilitation, intensive time commitment, and focus on creating a supportive intellectual community rather than remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive physical and social environment for minority programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Dedicated classroom spaces (e.g., MAP classroom), comfortable furniture, advisor areas, and environments where minorities are not isolated can contribute to program success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-technical features (comfort, safety to participate) are likely important intangible contributors to positive outcomes; consider dedicated spaces and staffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering strategy for minority students
rubrics_metrics.description: Clustering minority students in small dedicated sections with a highly regarded instructor committed to program goals can improve outcomes and create safer environments for participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select committed instructors, use small section sizes (≈30), and use positive evidence from pilot clusters to secure additional resources for wider adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: K-12 outreach program characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Outreach initiatives should include in-service teacher enhancement, curriculum design projects, policy engagement, and well-developed networks drawing on mathematicians, educators, policymakers, and community members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain year-round follow-up for teacher institutes, align programs with state frameworks (e.g., California Mathematics Framework), and include professional development with continued support (e-mail, follow-up).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional structures for outreach (centers and joint appointments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interdisciplinary centers and joint appointments (math-education) can serve as hubs for outreach and statewide initiatives (e.g., an interdisciplinary center directing Statewide Systemic Initiatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use centers to coordinate projects, bring together faculty and K-12 teachers, and provide administrative support for sustained outreach activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum design and scale-up impact
rubrics_metrics.description: University-developed curriculum projects (e.g., TIMS) that evolve into textbooks or scalable programs can extend faculty expertise into K-12 settings and have broad influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support curriculum projects that can produce tangible products (texts, materials) and plan for dissemination and evaluation of classroom impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridges between mathematics and education departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations should include joint grant roles (co-PI), inclusion of math-education faculty as evaluators of learning outcomes, and redesign of teacher-content courses to standards (e.g., NCTM Standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster joint appointments, involve math education faculty in technology grant evaluation and course redesign, and take teacher-certification requirements seriously in course planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental recognition/support for community-engaged faculty work
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments should value and, when appropriate, support faculty community efforts (e.g., outreach) rather than penalize them via research/teaching expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institutional backing (not necessarily reduced expectations) and recognize publicity and community benefit as legitimate departmental contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource adequacy for implementing reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgetary and resource constraints (e.g., inability to reduce class size) limit the extent to which structural reforms can be implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan reforms with realistic resource assessments, seek external funding or central administration support, and use pilot programs to demonstrate effectiveness for securing resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of external organizations (MER) in facilitating reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations like MER can facilitate balanced discussion, share experiences across departments, host workshops, and help conceptualize multi-institution proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external workshops to diffuse innovations, provide neutral forums for debate (not pushing single viewpoints), and maintain follow-up communication channels for sustained collaboration.
